key_insight: A variational, connectivity-aware quantum circuit can generate permutations uniformly exactly, even on linear nearest-neighbor hardware, with linear depth.
engineering_relevance: This lowers hardware connectivity demands and improves depth for exact uniform permutation sampling, making it more practical for near-term quantum devices.
method: Builds variational quantum circuits whose layout follows the device interaction graph.
Uses controlled-SWAP-based unitary constructions to enforce exact uniform permutation statistics.
Provides a linear-depth O(n) construction on linear nearest-neighbor topologies and analyzes a Beneš-like alternative.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports explicit exact constructions with quadratic circuit size and linear depth, and a proof that Beneš-like architectures cannot achieve uniform permutation distributions for any parameters.
watch_item: Exact uniformity may still be costly in circuit size and the parameter optimization must respect hardware noise and connectivity constraints.
paper_title: Variational Approach for Uniform Quantum Permutation Generators
